name: Scarface
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (FS Road 7601 off Icicle Creek Road), follow the Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599) — 4 miles, 2,280 ft gain, crossing Mountaineer Creek on a log bridge at 1.5 miles, staying right at the Lake Stuart Trail junction, finishing with a boulder-moraine climb to the outlet (2.5-3 hours). Top off water here. Head toward the lake's south/east side onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail, gaining talus/heather to about 400 ft above the lake (30-40 min, watch for wet snow into July), then cut climber's-left through dense slide-alder/heather brush (15-20 minutes) to the base gully system. Scarface climbs the gully just left of the West Face route's start; this terrain is very loose and exposed, so extra care with rope-up/spacing is warranted through the final approach scramble. Total trailhead-to-base time runs about 3.5-4 hours, in line with neighboring routes.

waypoints.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead (FR 7601)
waypoints.directions: From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto FR 7601 (Eightmile Road) and follow it about 4 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit at the trailhead. FR 7601 is gated closed from late fall through spring.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Lake outlet / north end
waypoints.directions: Hike the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 up Mountaineer Creek, crossing it on a log bridge at about 1.5 miles, and take the left fork onto the Colchuck Lake Trail at the junction. Climb the final boulder moraine to the lake's outlet at its north end, about 4 miles and 2,300 ft from the car. Fill water here.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Balanced Rock summit
waypoints.directions: Follow the trail counter-clockwise around the lake to its south end and onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail. At about 400 ft above the lake, cut climber's left through dense slide alder and heather to the gully system below the west face; the start is the gully just left of the West Face route, very loose and exposed. Climb the route's six pitches to the summit ridge.
